title: Retroactive salary clawback applied after 10 weeks of technical placement
summary: Illustrative anonymized case: After 10 consecutive weekly payslips paid at the rate agreed during onboarding, the payroll department applied a unilateral negative correction citing an internal rate reclassification, reducing net take-home pay below agreed terms without prior written consent.
timelineNotes:
Week 1: Signed placement confirmation and started technical assignment.
Weeks 1–10: Weekly payslips issued consistently at agreed hourly rate.
Week 11: Retroactive negative adjustment appeared on loonstrook without signed addendum.
Action taken: Sent written objection requesting itemized CAO calculation and prepared SNCU + Arbeidsinspectie dossier.

title: Two months of paid commute fuel retroactively clawed back from earned salary
summary: Illustrative anonymized case: For two consecutive months the transport and payroll desks paid commute fuel/petrol costs without issue. After completing those shifts, the agency declared the reimbursements an 'internal mistake' and deducted the entire 2-month fuel total directly out of earned net wages.
timelineNotes:
Months 1–2: Fuel/commute costs reimbursed consistently while driving to assigned workplace.
Month 3: Transport/payroll desk claimed prior fuel payouts were made in error and applied a lump-sum negative deduction to net salary.
Action taken: Preserved all payslips, fuel receipts, and transport messages; cited BW Art. 7:611 (good employership) and BW Art. 7:632 (wage set-off limits) for SNCU & legal counsel review.

title: Rodent infestation and unresolved sanitation defects in agency-deducted housing
summary: Illustrative anonymized case: Weekly housing charges were deducted directly from salary while shared kitchen and ground-floor bedrooms showed active rodent presence and dampness. Written maintenance tickets went unresolved for over three weeks.
timelineNotes:
Week 4: First written notice with timestamped kitchen/utility photos sent to housing portal.
Week 6: Second notice sent after no pest-control visit occurred.
Week 8: Verified SNF registration status and compiled SNF complaint + WAS 25% deduction check.

title: Mismatch between advertised gross rate and Phase A contract pay scale
summary: Illustrative anonymized case: Recruitment offer referenced host-company skilled scale, but onboarding contract placed the worker two tiers lower without documenting the host company's inlenersbeloning statement.
timelineNotes:
Pre-arrival: Received written job summary with target hourly gross rate.
Day 1: Signed digital contract under time pressure; scale differed from host-company peers.
Week 6: Requested formal inlenersbeloning overview under ABU/NBBU CAO and consulted Juridisch Loket.

title: ADV hours omitted while vakantie-uren booked into minus (-€890) to pressure continued work
summary: Illustrative anonymized case: On host-company ADV/closure days or lower-hour weeks, instead of applying host-company ADV hours (inlenersbeloning), the agency booked statutory holiday hours (vakantie-uren) into a negative balance, creating artificial debt to deter leaving or reduce final pay.
timelineNotes:
Weeks 1–12: Worked full technical schedule where permanent host-company staff accrued/used ADV hours.
Weeks 13–16: Payslip showed vakantie-uren pushed deep into minus without written employee leave requests.
Legal check: Cited BW Art. 7:638 (holiday hours set per worker's wish), BW Art. 7:628 (employer risk), BW Art. 7:632 (set-off ban), and ABU/NBBU CAO ADV parity for SNCU & counsel review.

title: Unanswered planning calls, unpaid guaranteed hours in housing & forced use of personal gear (-€1,150)
summary: Illustrative anonymized case: Despite a written weekly hours guarantee, the agency stopped scheduling shifts, ignored phone calls, left the worker in agency housing accumulating rent debt without pay, and previously required personal phone, car, and tools for work.
timelineNotes:
Weeks 1–3: Completed shifts while using personal phone/car and own work gear without reimbursement.
Weeks 4–5: Planning desk stopped assigning shifts and did not answer phone calls while housing charges continued.
Legal check: Sent written availability notice under BW Art. 7:628 (loondoorbetaling) + Arbowet PPE/equipment claim to SNCU, Arbeidsinspectie & Juridisch Loket.
